items:
[P0] 台灣就業通 no-figure wording is negotiable pay, never NT$40,000 (JT-1; strategy 1.3, 1.5; TW note 6 item 1)
CHANGE: server/src/features/jobs/normalize/salary.ts: NEGOTIABLE_RE (line 167) gains the Taiwan open-data wording: 依學經歷、證照核薪, 依學經歷, 核薪, plus the Simplified forms (依学经历, 核薪). In parseSalaryText (195-265) the existing order already scrubs TW_FLOOR_RE only when the text is negotiable (204-206); keep that order and make sure a text that matches the new alternatives returns { min: null, max: null, negotiable: true, text: verbatim } when nothing but the floor clause carried a number. payFromDescription / negotiablePhrase (309-331) accept the same wording so a description line reads the same way. Do not add a fallback that turns a floor clause into a minimum anywhere. server/src/features/jobs/sources/atsPublic/hooks.ts: TW_NEGOTIABLE_RE (line 75) gains the same alternatives so isTwNegotiable (98-100) is true for the sentence and twCardMeta marks pay.negotiable. Line numbers are from the tree before the parity wave merged; re-locate by function name.
ACCEPT: parseSalaryText('依學經歷、證照核薪(每月經常性薪資達4萬元以上)', { country: 'TW' }) returns no figure (min and max null), negotiable true and the verbatim text (the 'Accepted when' of JT-1); normalizeSalary for that text gives salaryDisclosed false, salaryMin null, salaryAnnualMin null; a real figure next to the wording ('月薪 45,000~60,000，依學經歷核薪') still parses to 45,000-60,000 TWD a month with negotiable false; no existing salary test changes its expectation.
TESTS: server/src/features/jobs/normalize/salary.test.ts: the sentence above (with half-width and full-width brackets), the three new alternatives alone, the figure-plus-wording case, a description line carrying the sentence (payFromDescription). server/src/features/jobs/sources/atsPublic/atsPublic.test.ts: twCardMeta on a Taiwan job whose salaryText is the sentence gives pay.negotiable true, pay.disclosed false and a card text without any amount.
FILES: server/src/features/jobs/normalize/salary.ts, server/src/features/jobs/normalize/salary.test.ts, server/src/features/jobs/sources/atsPublic/hooks.ts, server/src/features/jobs/sources/atsPublic/atsPublic.test.ts

[P0] The Art. 5 floor clause is recognised at any threshold (JT-1; strategy 1.3; TW note 4, 6 item 6)
CHANGE: The Ministry of Labor has announced a move from NT$40,000 to about NT$50,000 (not passed), so both regexes stop hard-coding 4. server/src/features/jobs/normalize/salary.ts TW_FLOOR_RE (170-171): the amount alternative becomes one of [4-9] or the Chinese numerals 四五六七八九 followed by 萬 / 万 (with optional 元), or [4-9]0,000 / [4-9]0000 (with optional 元), each followed by the existing optional 或 and 以上; keep both digit look-behinds exactly as they are so '104萬以上' and '140,000以上' are still real figures; keep the optional leading 經常性 / 薪資 / 月薪 / 達 / 新台幣 / NT$ parts. server/src/features/jobs/sources/atsPublic/hooks.ts TW_FLOOR_CLAUSE_RE (82-87): the same generalisation (it already accepts full-width digits: extend the class to ４-９ and the zero forms). The clause is removed only from a negotiable posting's card text (twNegotiableCardText, 92-95) and scrubbed only when the pay text is negotiable (salary.ts 206); a non-negotiable '月薪5萬以上' stays a disclosed minimum of 50,000. No constant named after 40,000 remains in either file; comments say 'the statutory threshold'.
ACCEPT: '待遇面議（經常性薪資達5萬元或以上）' parses to no figure and negotiable true, and twNegotiableCardText returns '待遇面議' (the 'a 5萬 clause is removed from card text' line of JT-1); the same holds for 4萬, 6萬, '50,000元以上' and full-width digits; '月薪 5萬以上' without negotiable wording is min 50,000 TWD month; '104萬以上' is untouched; the threshold is never produced as a job's pay by any path.
TESTS: server/src/features/jobs/normalize/salary.test.ts: a table of clause variants (4-9 萬, 40,000-90,000, Chinese numerals, full-width) crossed with negotiable / not negotiable; the two look-behind guards. server/src/features/jobs/sources/atsPublic/atsPublic.test.ts: twNegotiableCardText for 4萬, 5萬 and a posting with no clause.
FILES: server/src/features/jobs/normalize/salary.ts, server/src/features/jobs/normalize/salary.test.ts, server/src/features/jobs/sources/atsPublic/hooks.ts, server/src/features/jobs/sources/atsPublic/atsPublic.test.ts

[P0] Provider ids, adapter options and input fields the M2 and M3 source bundles compile against (JI-2, JT-2, JT-4, JT-9, JI-9, JI-7; strategy 1.2-1.5)
CHANGE: Types and inert defaults only, so bundles that run in parallel later do not need each other's files. (1) server/src/features/jobs/normalize/types.ts: NormalizeProvider (line 13) becomes JobProvider | 'ats_public' | 'tw_open_data' | 'tw_gov_jobs' | 'usajobs' | 'activejobs_feed' (no edit to server/src/platform/brand/registry.ts). ProviderJobInput (66-141) gains optional taxonomyId?: string | null (the source's own occupation code already mapped to a taxonomy L3 id), sponsorshipProvider?: 'offered' | 'not_offered' | null (a provider's reading, never a fact), locationDistrict?: string | null and workShift?: string | null. NormalizeContext (143-163) gains optional companyDomains?: ReadonlyMap<string, string> (companyNameNormalized -> the employer's registrable domain; read by the dedupe key in MKT-J4, filled by the pipeline in MKT-J2; unused until then). FieldSource already has 'provider'. (2) server/src/features/jobs/normalize/source.ts PROVIDER_META (31-39) gains entries: tw_open_data { sourcePriority 12, sourceBoard 'tw_open_data', aggregatorName '台灣就業通', applicantCountAllowed false, fromRecruiterBank false }, tw_gov_jobs { 12, 'tw_gov_jobs', '事求人', false, false }, usajobs { 8, 'usajobs', 'USAJOBS', false, false }, activejobs_feed { 10, 'activejobs', 'Active Jobs DB', true, false } (the feed writes the same sourceBoard as the search adapter, so both address the same rows; check every reverse lookup from a sourceBoard to a provider id (search for PROVIDER_META usages) and keep 'activejobs' resolving to the search provider). Priorities of existing providers do not change in this bundle. (3) server/src/features/jobs/normalize/normalizeProviderJob.ts (taxonomy step, 168-172): when raw.taxonomyId is a valid L3 id (isTaxonomyId and level 3) it becomes the primary taxonomy id with its ancestors and fieldSources.taxonomy = 'provider'; otherwise the title dictionary runs as today. Nothing reads the other three new fields yet. (4) server/src/features/jobs/sources/types.ts JobSourceAdapter (83-100) gains two optional members: costModel?: 'free' | 'per_job' | 'per_request' and isEnabledFor?(market): boolean; export adapterCostModel(adapter) (declared value, else jsearch -> per_request, activejobs / activejobs_feed / linkedin -> per_job, everything else free) and adapterEnabledFor(adapter, market) (isEnabledFor when present, else isEnabled; never throws). IngestQueryParams.q is documented as 'role text in the query language (English, or Traditional Chinese for a Taiwan variant)'. (5) server/src/features/jobs/taxonomy/taxonomy.ts TaxonomyNode (26-37) gains optional zhHant?: string and synonyms.zhHant?: string[]; taxonomyLabel (118-122) returns node.zhHant for locale 'zh-TW' when it is set, else the English label as today (the data arrives in MKT-J6).
ACCEPT: npm run typecheck:server passes with every Record<NormalizeProvider, …> filled; normalizeProviderJob with taxonomyId 'software_engineer' and an unrelated title returns that primary id with source 'provider', and with an unknown id falls back to the title match; adapterCostModel of the registered jsearch adapter is per_request and of ats_public is free; taxonomyLabel(id, 'zh-TW') still returns English for today's data and returns the zhHant label for a node fixture that has one; no behaviour of an existing provider changes (the normalizer snapshot tests are unchanged).
TESTS: server/src/features/jobs/normalize/normalizeProviderJob.test.ts (taxonomyId accepted / rejected, the four new providers normalise a minimal input with the right sourceBoard and priority), server/src/features/jobs/taxonomy/taxonomy.test.ts (zh-TW label with and without zhHant), a new server/src/features/jobs/sources/types.test.ts for adapterCostModel and adapterEnabledFor (declared value, defaults by provider id, a throwing isEnabled).

[P1] Provider quota snapshot contract and the identifying User-Agent (JI-1, JI-4; strategy 1.2 tier 0, 1.3; critic C13)
CHANGE: (1) New server/src/features/jobs/ingest/quotaContract.ts (types, constants and a pure parser; no database or network code): PROVIDER_QUOTA_CONFIG_KEY = 'jobs.providerQuota.v1' (an AppConfig row, value = JSON text; RAProviderUsage has no column for it and is not changed). Shape: { version: 1, providers: { [provider: string]: ProviderQuotaSnapshot } } with ProviderQuotaSnapshot = { provider, plan: string | null (only a name the provider itself stated, e.g. 'BASIC' read from a 429 body; never guessed), requestsLimit, requestsRemaining, jobsLimit, jobsRemaining (numbers or null), resetAt: ISO string | null, observedAt: ISO string, lastStatus: number | null, lastCallCost: number | null (requests the last call consumed, from the header delta), state: 'ok' | 'exhausted' | 'not_subscribed' | 'unauthorized' | 'unknown' }. Export parseProviderQuota(raw: string | null | undefined) (tolerant: bad JSON or a wrong version gives an empty map), serializeProviderQuota, daysToReset(snapshot, now) (null without resetAt; 0 when past) and usageKey(provider, market) = provider for 'intl' and provider + ':cn' for 'cn' (daily usage for mainland calls is counted under that key, C13). (2) New server/src/features/jobs/sources/userAgent.ts: sourceUserAgent(market, env) returns 'RoboApplyJobs/1.0 (+<contact>)' for intl and 'GoApplyJobs/1.0 (+<contact>)' for cn, where contact is env JOB_SOURCES_CONTACT (a URL or mailto) and otherwise the brand's canonical site URL from the brand registry; the value is sanitised to printable ASCII without CR / LF and capped at 200 characters. Every adapter that reads a public job-board or open-data endpoint sends it.
ACCEPT: parseProviderQuota round-trips a snapshot written by serializeProviderQuota and returns an empty map for '', 'x' and { version: 2 }; daysToReset is 17 for a reset 16.9 days ahead (rounded up) and 0 for a past reset; usageKey('activejobs','cn') is 'activejobs:cn'; sourceUserAgent('intl', {}) names RoboApply and the roboapply.io origin, with JOB_SOURCES_CONTACT set it carries that value, and a value containing a line break is cleaned.
TESTS: server/src/features/jobs/ingest/quotaContract.test.ts and server/src/features/jobs/sources/userAgent.test.ts (pure unit tests; no network, no database).
FILES: server/src/features/jobs/ingest/quotaContract.ts, server/src/features/jobs/ingest/quotaContract.test.ts, server/src/features/jobs/sources/userAgent.ts, server/src/features/jobs/sources/userAgent.test.ts
env: JOB_SOURCES_CONTACT: contact URL or mailto printed in the User-Agent of every job-board and open-data request (default: the brand site URL)

bundles.title: Ingest core: monthly quota from response headers, one budget per provider, JSearch as a demand-only source
items:
[P0] Monthly quota read from every RapidAPI response and stored in AppConfig (JI-1; strategy 1.1, 1.2; INTL note 8.1 M1)
CHANGE: New server/src/features/jobs/ingest/quota.ts on top of MKT-J1's quotaContract.ts. (1) Capture: server/src/roboapply/v2/lib/raRapidApiJobs.ts already reads x-ratelimit-requests-limit / -remaining / -reset after a response (510-512) and decides monthly 429s in isMonthlyQuota429 (378-381); server/src/roboapply/v2/lib/raFantasticJobs.ts reads the same two request headers (596-597). Both clients export setQuotaListener(listener | null) and call it once per upstream response (success, 429, 401, 403; not for cache hits) with { provider: 'jsearch' | 'activejobs' | 'linkedin', status, requestsLimit, requestsRemaining, resetSeconds, jobsLimit, jobsRemaining (x-ratelimit-jobs-limit / x-ratelimit-jobs-remaining when the response carries them, else null), plan (the token after 'current plan,' in a 429 body such as '…on your current plan, BASIC', else null), at }. A listener that throws is swallowed; the key is never passed. (2) quota.ts keeps the latest snapshot per provider in memory, derives state (429 with remaining 0 -> 'exhausted'; 403 'not subscribed' -> 'not_subscribed'; 401 -> 'unauthorized'; a 2xx -> 'ok'), computes resetAt = at + resetSeconds and lastCallCost = previous remaining minus new remaining when both are known and the previous observation is under 60 s old, and persists the whole map to AppConfig key jobs.providerQuota.v1 (upsert, as platform/billing/fxReference.ts does for fx.reference): at once on a state change, otherwise at most once every 60 s per provider. hydrateProviderQuota(db) loads the stored map into memory (a stored snapshot whose resetAt has passed is treated as 'unknown' with remaining null until a new response arrives); it is called at the start of runJobsPlan and runJobsIngest (server/src/features/jobs/ingest/cron.ts 54-73), of the ingest.query worker path and of ingestForProfile (server/src/features/jobs/ingest/index.ts 54-58). registerQuotaListeners() wires the two clients; server/src/features/jobs/ingest/index.ts and server/src/features/jobs/ingest/cron.ts import quota.ts for that side effect, and server/src/cron/handlers.ts already imports ingest/cron.js at process start, so interactive callers of the clients (onboarding chat, the Assistant, the job-search API) are covered on every deployment without importing ingest themselves. (3) Read API for the rest of ingest: quotaSnapshot(provider), quotaAllows(provider, purpose: 'ingest' | 'interactive', now, env): ingest is refused while state is exhausted / not_subscribed / unauthorized and resetAt is in the future, or while requestsRemaining <= reserve where reserve = max(1, ceil(requestsLimit x INGEST_QUOTA_RESERVE_SHARE)) (default share 0.05); interactive use (onboarding, Assistant, the job-search API) is refused only at remaining 0 or a closed state. With no snapshot both are allowed.
ACCEPT: The 'Accepted when' of JI-1, server half: a mocked 429 whose headers say remaining 0 and reset in 16.9 days writes state 'exhausted', plan 'BASIC' and resetAt to AppConfig, quotaAllows(provider,'ingest') is false until that instant and true after it; a 200 with remaining 9,773 of 10,000 gives state ok and lastCallCost equal to the delta from the previous response; a 403 not-subscribed response gives not_subscribed; nothing is written more than once a minute for an unchanged state; a second process that only calls hydrateProviderQuota sees the same answer without any provider call; the RapidAPI key never appears in a snapshot or a log line.
TESTS: server/src/features/jobs/ingest/quota.test.ts with a fake AppConfig delegate and a fixed clock: state derivation, reserve arithmetic, debounce, hydrate, expiry of a stale snapshot. server/src/roboapply/v2/lib/raRapidApiJobs.test.ts and raFantasticJobs.test.ts with a mocked fetch: the listener receives the header values for 200 / 429 / 403, not for a cache hit, and a throwing listener does not fail the search.
FILES: server/src/features/jobs/ingest/quota.ts, server/src/features/jobs/ingest/quota.test.ts, server/src/features/jobs/ingest/cron.ts, server/src/features/jobs/ingest/index.ts, server/src/features/jobs/ingest/workers.ts, server/src/roboapply/v2/lib/raRapidApiJobs.ts, server/src/roboapply/v2/lib/raRapidApiJobs.test.ts, server/src/roboapply/v2/lib/raFantasticJobs.ts, server/src/roboapply/v2/lib/raFantasticJobs.test.ts

[P0] One budget per provider: the quota gates planning, leasing and every client call; mainland calls are counted under :cn (JI-1, JC-6 preparation; strategy 1.2; critic C13) CHANGE: Today two independent counters exist: ingest's RAProviderUsage budget (server/src/features/jobs/ingest/pipeline.ts reserveProviderCall 209-217, used in runIngestQuery 312-322 with DEFAULT_DAILY_CALLS 300 / 150 / 200 in config.ts 23-27) and an in-process daily budget inside each client (raRapidApiJobs.ts dailyBudget 344-348, default 300; raFantasticJobs.ts 41 and 323-324). Replace them with one. (1) server/src/features/jobs/ingest/config.ts: effectiveDailyLimit(provider, market, env, now) = the smaller of INGEST__DAILY_CALLS (when set; RA_ONBOARDING_

_DAILY_BUDGET is read as a deprecated alias when the INGEST name is unset, logged once) and, when a snapshot with requestsRemaining and resetAt exists, floor((requestsRemaining - reserve) / max(1, daysToReset)); without env and without a snapshot the old defaults apply. For market 'cn' the limit is INGEST__CN_DAILY_CALLS (default 0: nothing is called for GoApply until MKT-J9 opens Active Jobs DB behind its quota gate). dailyCallLimit(provider) stays exported for the admin Limits page. (2) pipeline.ts runIngestQuery: before reserving, when the adapter is metered and quotaAllows(provider,'ingest') is false, push every due query of that provider to the quota's resetAt (or one hour ahead when resetAt is unknown) with buildDeferProviderSql (255-261) and return status 'quota' (a new QueryRunResult status; run.ts addToTally lists the provider in budgetStops and drops it for the tick like 'budget'). Reservation and usage rows use usageKey(provider, ctx.market) and effectiveDailyLimit; adapter enablement uses adapterEnabledFor(adapter, ctx.market) at line 308. (3) Clients: delete the in-process daily counters and their warn-once state; each client exports setCallGate(gate | null) where gate(provider, purpose) returns false to refuse a call; quota.ts registers a gate that answers quotaAllows(...) and, for calls not made by ingest, records one call in RAProviderUsage through recordProviderUsage. JobSearchProvider.search opts (server/src/roboapply/v2/lib/raExternalJobTypes.ts 142-149) gain reservedByIngest?: boolean; the ingest adapter (server/src/features/jobs/ingest/adapters/rapidApi.ts fetch, 106-116) passes true so an ingest call is counted once. isJSearchEnabled / isFantasticJobsEnabled consult the gate for 'interactive'. The LRU caches, circuit breakers and kill switches stay. (4) Fairness for cursor sources (strategy 1.3 time budget, C12): server/src/features/jobs/ingest/run.ts runIngestTick (71-110) tracks milliseconds spent per cursor provider in the tick; a cursor provider that keeps answering 'more' is dropped from the tick's enabled map once it has used more than INGEST_CURSOR_TICK_SHARE (default 0.4) of budgetMs, so a multi-run sweep (台灣就業通, the licensed feed) cannot starve users' demand queries; its query stays due and continues on the next tick. ACCEPT: With a snapshot of 25 requests a month and 0 left, a jobs-ingest tick makes no Active Jobs DB call, defers its due queries to the reset time and reports the provider under budgetStops; with 9,773 of 10,000 JSearch requests left and 17 days to reset the effective daily limit is 545 (floor((9773 - 500) / 17)) unless INGEST_JSEARCH_DAILY_CALLS is lower; an onboarding search and an ingest query in the same day add up in one RAProviderUsage row; a query run for GoApply is counted under 'activejobs:cn' and is refused while INGEST_ACTIVEJOBS_CN_DAILY_CALLS is unset; no file still holds a second, client-local daily counter; a cursor adapter that always answers 'more' stops after about 40% of a tick and the remaining queries of the tick still run. TESTS: server/src/features/jobs/ingest/pipeline.test.ts (quota stop defers by provider, the :cn key, single counting with reservedByIngest), server/src/features/jobs/ingest/cron.test.ts (a tick with an exhausted provider), a new case in pipeline.test.ts or run tests for the cursor share with a fake clock, the two client test files (gate refuses, gate allows, cache hit bypasses the gate), server/src/features/jobs/ingest/adapters/adapters.test.ts (the adapter passes reservedByIngest). Update the SQL snapshots under ingest/__snapshots__ only where the usage key parameter changed. FILES: server/src/features/jobs/ingest/config.ts, server/src/features/jobs/ingest/pipeline.ts, server/src/features/jobs/ingest/pipeline.test.ts, server/src/features/jobs/ingest/run.ts, server/src/features/jobs/ingest/cron.test.ts, server/src/features/jobs/ingest/quota.ts, server/src/features/jobs/ingest/adapters/rapidApi.ts, server/src/features/jobs/ingest/adapters/adapters.test.ts, server/src/roboapply/v2/lib/raRapidApiJobs.ts, server/src/roboapply/v2/lib/raFantasticJobs.ts, server/src/roboapply/v2/lib/raExternalJobTypes.ts, their tests and server/src/features/jobs/ingest/__snapshots__/*.snap

[P0] JSearch client: employer-direct is decided by the link host (JI-6; strategy M-3; INTL note 3.1, 8.1 M7)
CHANGE: The 2026-10-11 probes found one apply option per job and is_direct true on 0 of 58 rows, so server/src/roboapply/v2/lib/raRapidApiJobs.ts pickApplyUrl (164-170) cannot work as written. Rewrite it as a host rule using atsTypeFromUrl and isJobBoardHost from server/src/features/jobs/normalize/index.ts (roboapply/v2/lib already imports that module in raCrossBankMatch.ts): collect job_apply_link and every apply_options[].apply_link that is a valid http(s) URL; choose, in order, the first link on an ATS host or an unknown employer host (atsTypeFromUrl not null), then the first link on a job board that is not LinkedIn, then a LinkedIn link; isDirect is true exactly when the chosen link is on an ATS or employer host (an explicit is_direct / job_apply_is_direct true is still honoured). pickSourceUrl (173-188) keeps the publisher page for provenance. normalizeJSearchJob (194-248) passes the result through unchanged otherwise. Nothing may depend on job_highlights (empty on every probed row): confirm by search that no reader requires it and delete any dead read. Keep num_pages 2 (line 450); the cost of the second page is now visible as lastCallCost in the quota snapshot, so do not change paging in this bundle. The rule that a row whose only link is LinkedIn or Indeed is not ingested lives in the normalizer (MKT-J4); this client still returns such rows to interactive callers, who already hide LinkedIn links.
ACCEPT: The 'employer-host link is marked direct' half of JI-6: a fixture row whose single link is boards.greenhouse.io/acme/jobs/1 has applyIsDirect true; a row with a LinkedIn link and a careers.acme.com option applies on careers.acme.com with applyIsDirect true and keeps the LinkedIn page only as sourceUrl provenance (which the normalizer then drops from every source field); a row with only a ZipRecruiter link is not direct; a row with empty apply_options and is_direct false everywhere behaves as before for the URL and gets the host-derived flag.
TESTS: server/src/roboapply/v2/lib/raRapidApiJobs.test.ts: the four link shapes above from fixtures modelled on the probe counts (no live call), plus a row with an invalid URL in apply_options.
FILES: server/src/roboapply/v2/lib/raRapidApiJobs.ts, server/src/roboapply/v2/lib/raRapidApiJobs.test.ts

[P1] JSearch query building for Taiwan: Traditional Chinese text with language=zh-TW (JT-3; strategy 1.3, 2.5; TW note 5.1)
CHANGE: server/src/features/jobs/ingest/adapters/rapidApi.ts rapidApiSearchParams (46-61) builds '<q> in <city>' for every JSearch query and never sets language, so Taiwan demand is searched in English and returns a LinkedIn-heavy mix. Change, for provider 'jsearch' only: when the resolved country (rapidApiCountry, 32-40) is TW and params.q contains a CJK character, the query is '<q> <city in Traditional Chinese>' (the city table's zhHant name from findCity / citiesNamed; the English name when the table has none) with no ' in ' joiner, and language = 'zh-TW'; otherwise the English form stays and no language is sent. datePosted is passed through as planned (the planner sends 'month' for Taiwan, MKT-J3); 'remote' keeps work_from_home. Active Jobs DB keeps the English title and location name (it searches English ATS postings). The planner side (two tuples per Taiwan role) is MKT-J3; this function must give the right request for either text.
ACCEPT: rapidApiSearchParams({ q: '軟體工程師', country: 'TW', city: 'Taipei', datePosted: 'month' }, 'jsearch') returns query '軟體工程師 台北', country 'tw', language 'zh-TW', datePosted 'month'; the English tuple for the same role returns 'software engineer in Taipei' with no language; a Chinese query for a non-Taiwan country is not given language zh-TW; the existing WP-42 assertion (a Taiwanese city forces country=tw) still passes.
TESTS: server/src/features/jobs/ingest/adapters/adapters.test.ts: the three cases above and a city missing from the table.
FILES: server/src/features/jobs/ingest/adapters/rapidApi.ts, server/src/features/jobs/ingest/adapters/adapters.test.ts

[P1] Known employer domains reach the normalizer, page by page (JI-5 support; strategy 1.5 K3)
CHANGE: server/src/features/jobs/ingest/pipeline.ts processJobs (71-172): before the normalize loop build companyDomains: ReadonlyMap<string, string> for the page and pass it in the NormalizeContext (the optional field MKT-J1 declared; MKT-J4 reads it when it builds the dedupe key). Sources of the map, in this order: (1) domains the page's own inputs state (input.companyFacts.domain, or the host of companyFacts.website) keyed by the normalised company name (use normalizeCompanyName from server/src/features/jobs/normalize/index.ts, the same function the normalizer uses); (2) one query for the remaining names of the page: SELECT "nameNormalized", "domain" FROM "RACompany" WHERE "market" = ctx.market AND "nameNormalized" = ANY(names) AND "domain" IS NOT NULL. The map carries the hosts as stored or stated (RACompany.domain is the stated domain or the website's host, unfiltered); MKT-J4's key logic reduces each value to a registrable domain and rejects job-board and ATS hosts, so this function does no host filtering beyond dropping empty values. One extra read per page; no write. Nothing else in processJobs changes: the apply-URL rule (125-128), the wrong_market rule (129-133) and the applyDedupe call (166) stay as they are.
ACCEPT: For a page with two inputs of the same normalised company, one of which states the website, both normalize calls receive that domain; a company whose RACompany row already has a domain is looked up once per page, not once per row; a page of 100 rows makes exactly one extra query; with no domain known anywhere the context carries an empty map and the output is identical to before.
TESTS: server/src/features/jobs/ingest/pipeline.test.ts with the fake db: the map content for the three sources and the single query.
FILES: server/src/features/jobs/ingest/pipeline.ts, server/src/features/jobs/ingest/pipeline.test.ts
env: INGEST_QUOTA_RESERVE_SHARE: share of a provider's monthly request limit that ingest leaves for interactive searches (0.05)
INGEST_<PROVIDER>_DAILY_CALLS: upper bound of the daily call budget; the effective budget is also capped by remaining quota / days to reset (existing defaults)
INGEST_<PROVIDER>_CN_DAILY_CALLS: daily call budget for GoApply, counted under <provider>:cn (0)
INGEST_CURSOR_TICK_SHARE: share of one ingest tick a single cursor source may use (0.4)

bundles.title: Planner: adapter cost model, no SEO seeds on per-request providers, demand windows, Taiwan query variants
items:
[P0] SEO seed tuples are planned only on sources that cost nothing per request (JI-2; strategy M-3, 1.2; INTL note 6.3, 8.1 M2)
CHANGE: server/src/features/jobs/ingest/planner.ts planQueries (197-217) plans one query per search adapter for every tuple, so the default 900 seed tuples (300 roles x 3 cities, seedTuples 136-150) are multiplied onto JSearch, a provider billed per request with a monthly quota. Change: for a tuple with origin 'seo_seed', skip every adapter whose adapterCostModel (MKT-J1, server/src/features/jobs/sources/types.ts) is 'per_request'; demand tuples are unaffected. runPlanner (337-352) then retires what earlier plans created: one statement sets enabled = false for RAIngestQuery rows with origin 'seo_seed' whose provider is a per_request adapter of this market (retireSeedsFor(db, market, providers), reported as seedsRetired in PlannerResult). Seeds for free and per-job sources stay as they are; while no such search adapter is enabled the seed tuples simply plan nothing (board sync and the bank need no query). Declare costModel explicitly where this bundle owns the adapter list: the source registry added by the parity wave (server/src/features/jobs/sources/registry.ts) exposes costModel per source so the admin console can show it. Update the planner header comment (lines 3-16) and the test names that say 'one query per provider'.
ACCEPT: The 'Accepted when' of JI-2: with default env, the RoboApply adapter list of the parity wave (activejobs, bank_robohire, jsearch, ats_public; linkedin already removed by PAR-1) and a brand with no users, runPlanner plans zero JSearch queries and zero LinkedIn queries; a demand tuple still plans a JSearch query; a database that holds old JSearch seed queries has them disabled after one plan run and a second run changes nothing; seeds remain planned for a per_job search adapter that is enabled.
TESTS: server/src/features/jobs/ingest/planner.test.ts: planQueries with a per_request, a per_job and a free fake adapter for seed and demand tuples; retireSeedsFor SQL through the fake db; the PlannerResult counters. server/src/features/jobs/sources/registry.test.ts: costModel is reported for every registered source.

[P0] A provider that is unsubscribed, out of quota or off for the market is not planned (JI-2; strategy 1.1; INTL note 1 item 2)
CHANGE: The planner created LinkedIn queries for an API that answers 403 and Active Jobs DB queries for a plan with 25 requests a month. In planQueries and in ensureBankSyncQueries (308-324) use adapterEnabledFor(adapter, tuple.market) from MKT-J1 instead of the bare markets check: an adapter that reports disabled (no key, kill switch, breaker open after a 403 / 401, or the quota gate of MKT-J2 closed) gets no new or refreshed query in this run, and its existing queries are left alone (they are deferred at lease time by MKT-J2, not disabled, so they resume when the quota resets). server/src/features/jobs/ingest/providers.ts adaptersForBrand (44-51): keep the parity wave's registry order; add listEnabledAdaptersFor(brand, env) used by cron and by the targeted ingest so both apply the same rule. Remove the special case at planner.ts line 205 ('GoApply testing provider: country=cn only') only if the parity wave left it behind; GoApply has no per-request search provider. server/src/roboapply/v2/lib/raJobProviders.ts: the registry comment (76-86) and externalProviders order are updated to the two remaining RapidAPI providers when PAR-1 removed linkedin from the brand list; if the linkedin client object is still exported, enabledExternalProviders must not return it for RoboApply (it is unsubscribed and dropped by decision M-4).
ACCEPT: With the Active Jobs DB adapter reporting disabled, a plan run writes no activejobs query and reports the provider in a new PlannerResult.skippedProviders list; when the adapter is enabled again the next run plans it; the parity acceptance 'adaptersForBrand(goapply) never includes jsearch' still holds; searchAllProviders never calls a LinkedIn client for a RoboApply request.
TESTS: server/src/features/jobs/ingest/planner.test.ts (disabled adapter, market-specific isEnabledFor), server/src/roboapply/v2/lib/raJobProviders.test.ts (provider list and fan-out without linkedin).
FILES: server/src/features/jobs/ingest/planner.ts, server/src/features/jobs/ingest/planner.test.ts, server/src/features/jobs/ingest/providers.ts, server/src/roboapply/v2/lib/raJobProviders.ts, server/src/roboapply/v2/lib/raJobProviders.test.ts

[P1] Demand queries ask for a window that matches their refresh interval (JI-6; strategy 1.2 tier 2; INTL note 6.3, 6.5)
CHANGE: server/src/features/jobs/ingest/planner.ts paramsForTuple (188-194) sends datePosted 'week' for every tuple while hot tuples refresh every 6 hours (REFRESH 33-42). Make the window a function of the tuple: demandScore >= 5 (refreshed every 6 h) -> '3days'; other demand tuples (12 h) -> 'week'; remote tuples keep remote: true so the JSearch adapter sends work_from_home; Taiwan tuples -> 'month' (next item). Because datePosted is part of paramsHash (178-186), a tuple that moves between hot and cold would otherwise leave a stale twin: plan with the hash of the tuple identity (market, taxonomy id or text, country, city, remote, query language) and treat datePosted as a mutable param that upsertPlannedQueries (265-289) updates in place (extend the ON CONFLICT clause to set "params" = EXCLUDED."params" while keeping any stored cursor). One migration-free consequence: queries created before this change keep their old hash and retire through retireUnusedDemand (296-305) as nobody plans them again. Never plan a JSearch query whose window is shorter than its refresh interval.
ACCEPT: A tuple with 6 users plans datePosted '3days'; with 2 users 'week'; raising a tuple from 2 to 6 users updates the same RAIngestQuery row to '3days' instead of creating a second row; a remote tuple carries remote true; the window always covers at least one full refresh interval.
TESTS: server/src/features/jobs/ingest/planner.test.ts: window by demand score, hash stability across a hot / cold change, the upsert statement keeps the cursor of a cursor query.
FILES: server/src/features/jobs/ingest/planner.ts, server/src/features/jobs/ingest/planner.test.ts

[P1] Taiwan demand is planned twice: once in Traditional Chinese, once in English, both over a month (JT-3, SM-11; strategy 1.3, 2.5; TW note 5.1)
CHANGE: In tuplesFromFilters / primaryRole (95-133) and paramsForTuple: for a tuple whose country is TW (or whose city is a Taiwanese city) plan two queries on per-request search adapters that take free text (jsearch): variant A with q = the taxonomy node's zhHant label (MKT-J1 added the optional field; MKT-J6 fills it) and variant B with q = the English label; both with datePosted 'month' (a one-week non-tech query returned 0 rows in the probe). When the role is the user's own typed title, plan it as typed, in whichever script it is in, plus nothing else. When a node has no zhHant label yet, plan only the English variant (never a Simplified label for Taiwan). The city stays the city-table English name in params; MKT-J2's rapidApiSearchParams turns it into the Traditional Chinese name for the Chinese variant. The tuple key and paramsHash include the query text so the two variants are two rows. Mainland tuples (market cn) use the zh label; nothing is planned for them until a search adapter is enabled for cn (MKT-J9). This item is the planner half of SM-11's 'zh / zhHant query labels'.
ACCEPT: The 'Accepted when' of JT-3: a Taiwan demand tuple for a role with a zhHant label plans exactly one zh-Hant JSearch query and one English JSearch query, both datePosted 'month'; without a zhHant label only the English one; a United States tuple plans one English query with the window of the previous item; an Active Jobs DB adapter gets the English variant only.
TESTS: server/src/features/jobs/ingest/planner.test.ts with a taxonomy node fixture that carries zhHant and one that does not.
FILES: server/src/features/jobs/ingest/planner.ts, server/src/features/jobs/ingest/planner.test.ts

items:
[P0] atsPostingKey: the exact key {ats}:{tenant}:{postingId} parsed from apply and source URLs (JI-5; strategy 1.5 K2; INTL note 7.1)
CHANGE: server/src/features/jobs/normalize/ats.ts: add atsPostingKeyFromUrl(url) and atsPostingKeyFromUrls(applyUrl, sourceUrl) returning '<ats>:<tenant>:<postingId>' in lower case (the posting id keeps its case when the ATS id is case-sensitive: Workable shortcodes and Ashby / Lever UUIDs are lower-cased, numeric ids are digits) or null. Patterns, each verified by a unit test on real URL shapes from the notes: Greenhouse boards.greenhouse.io/{token}/jobs/{id} and job-boards.greenhouse.io/{token}/jobs/{id} (an employer page that only carries ?gh_jid={id} gives null: the tenant is not in the URL and is never guessed); Lever jobs.lever.co/{site}/{uuid} -> lever:{site}:{uuid}, jobs.eu.lever.co/{site}/{uuid} -> lever_eu:{site}:{uuid}; Ashby jobs.ashbyhq.com/{org}/{uuid}; SmartRecruiters jobs.smartrecruiters.com/{company}/{id} (the id is the leading digits of the last path segment); Workable apply.workable.com/{slug}/j/{shortcode}; Workday {tenant}.wd{n}.myworkdayjobs.com/…/job/…/{slug}_{requisitionId} -> workday:{tenant}:{requisitionId}; iCIMS {sub}.icims.com/jobs/{id}/… -> icims:{sub}:{id}. Also extend ATS_HOSTS (10-24) and the AtsType union in server/src/features/jobs/normalize/types.ts with recruitee ((^|.)recruitee.com), personio ((^|.)jobs.personio.(de|com)), teamtailor ((^|.)teamtailor.com) and bamboohr ((^|.)bamboohr.com), so links to those boards are classified now (their connectors are MKT-J10) and the RAJob.atsType doc comment lists them. server/src/features/jobs/normalize/normalizeProviderJob.ts computes atsPostingKey next to atsType (line 200) for every provider; for ats_public rows it must equal '<sourceBoard>:<boardToken>:<postingId>' built from the row's own externalId (a test pins that the URL parse and the externalId agree for the four connectors). NormalizedJob gains atsPostingKey: string | null. server/src/features/jobs/ingest/upsert.ts: add the column to JobUpsertRow, UPSERT_COLUMNS (147-159), toUpsertRow (180-249), valuesTuple and the ON CONFLICT list (300-363) as "atsPostingKey" = EXCLUDED."atsPostingKey".
ACCEPT: A JSearch row whose link is boards.greenhouse.io/stripe/jobs/123 and the Greenhouse board row 'stripe:123' carry the same atsPostingKey 'greenhouse:stripe:123'; a careers page with only ?gh_jid= gives null; every pattern above has a positive and a negative test; an existing row is updated with its key on the next ingest; the upsert SQL snapshot shows the one new column and no other change.
TESTS: server/src/features/jobs/normalize/rules.test.ts or a new server/src/features/jobs/normalize/ats.test.ts (pattern table, hosts), server/src/features/jobs/normalize/normalizeProviderJob.test.ts (key on all providers; agreement with ats_public externalId), server/src/features/jobs/ingest/upsert.test.ts and its snapshot.
FILES: server/src/features/jobs/normalize/ats.ts, server/src/features/jobs/normalize/types.ts, server/src/features/jobs/normalize/normalizeProviderJob.ts, server/src/features/jobs/normalize/index.ts, their tests, server/src/features/jobs/ingest/upsert.ts, server/src/features/jobs/ingest/upsert.test.ts, server/src/features/jobs/ingest/__snapshots__/upsert.test.ts.snap

[P0] Canonical row: K2 before K3, employer board at priority 5, GoHire bank at priority 3, never across markets (JI-5, JC-7; strategy 1.5; critic C10)
CHANGE: (1) server/src/features/jobs/normalize/source.ts PROVIDER_META: ats_public sourcePriority 10 -> 5 (it tied with activejobs); bank_gohire 15 -> 3 (mainland order is GoHire bank > employer board > aggregator); bank_robohire stays 15. Update the comments in server/src/features/jobs/normalize/types.ts (NormalizedJob.sourcePriority) and the upsert header. (2) server/src/features/jobs/ingest/upsert.ts buildDedupeSql (421-442) / applyDedupe (444-447), without changing applyDedupe's signature (server/src/features/jobs/ingest/pipeline.ts line 166 keeps calling it with the page's dedupe keys): add a first statement that aligns exact twins: for live public rows of the market whose atsPostingKey equals that of any row carrying one of the given dedupe keys, set dedupeKey to the dedupeKey of the best row of that atsPostingKey group (lowest sourcePriority, then firstSeenAt, then id) where it differs; then run the existing ranking over the given keys plus the keys adopted in step one. The maintenance call (keys null) aligns every atsPostingKey group touched in the last two days. Both statements filter "market" = the given market, so rows in different markets never collapse (keep the existing WHERE; add a test that proves it). (3) Ranking order inside a group becomes: for Taiwan rows (locationCountry 'TW') a row with salaryDisclosed true first (twins from 台灣就業通 and from 104 through JSearch: prefer the row with disclosed pay); then sourcePriority ascending; then a row whose apply URL is on an employer or ATS host ("atsType" IS NOT NULL) before a job-board link; then postedAt descending nulls last, firstSeenAt, id (today's tail). Mirror the order in compareForCanonical (396-409) and DedupeCandidate. (4) server/src/features/jobs/ingest/maintain.ts: add alignSourcePriority(db, market), one idempotent UPDATE per changed provider that sets sourcePriority to the PROVIDER_META value for live rows that still carry the old number (sourceBoard in the four public ATS names and sourcePriority 10 -> 5; sourceBoard 'gohire' and 15 -> 3), run in runMaintenance (185-207) before the dedupe repair; report the count.
ACCEPT: The 'Accepted when' of JI-5: a JSearch row and a board row for the same Greenhouse posting collapse to one canonical board row even when their titles differ in wording; a GoHire bank row beats the same employer's board row for the same company, title and city; the same posting key in market intl and market cn stays two independent canonical rows; a Taiwan open-data row with pay beats a JSearch twin without pay; after one maintenance run no live ats row has priority 10 and no gohire row has 15; alternates stay live (no closeReason), as today.
TESTS: server/src/features/jobs/ingest/upsert.test.ts: compareForCanonical table (priority, Taiwan pay rule, employer-host tie-break), the two SQL statements in the snapshot, market isolation through the fake db. server/src/features/jobs/ingest/maintain.test.ts: alignSourcePriority statements and that a second run updates nothing. server/src/features/jobs/normalize/normalizeProviderJob.test.ts: the new priorities.
FILES: server/src/features/jobs/normalize/source.ts, server/src/features/jobs/normalize/types.ts, server/src/features/jobs/ingest/upsert.ts, server/src/features/jobs/ingest/upsert.test.ts, server/src/features/jobs/ingest/__snapshots__/upsert.test.ts.snap, server/src/features/jobs/ingest/maintain.ts, server/src/features/jobs/ingest/maintain.test.ts

[P1] The employer's domain replaces the company name in the fuzzy key when a source gives one (JI-5; strategy 1.5 K3; INTL note 7.1)
CHANGE: server/src/features/jobs/normalize/identity.ts dedupeKey (32-34) hashes companyNameNormalized | titleNormalized | place, so name variants agree only when the name normaliser happens to fold them and two different companies called 'Summit' collide. Rule: the company part of the key is the employer's registrable domain when one is known for the row, else the normalised name as today. A domain is known when (a) the source states it (raw.companyFacts.domain, or the host of raw.companyFacts.website) and that host is the employer's own (isJobBoardHost false and atsTypeFromUrl 'other': never an ATS or job-board host), or (b) NormalizeContext.companyDomains (the optional map nameNormalized -> domain that MKT-J1 declared and MKT-J2 fills from RACompany rows of the market and from the other rows of the same page) has an entry for the row's companyNameNormalized (the map carries raw hosts: pass every candidate through registrableDomain and the same employer-host test before use). With a domain the key is sha1('d:' + domain + '|' + titleNormalized + '|' + place); without one it is byte-identical to today's. Route (b) is what keeps a row that states no website on the same key as its twin that does. Add registrableDomain(urlOrHost) to server/src/features/jobs/normalize/company.ts: lower case, strip 'www.' and the career sub-domains careers., jobs., job., work., boards., apply., recruiting.; keep the last two labels, or the last three for these two-part suffixes: co.uk, com.au, com.sg, com.tw, co.jp, com.cn, com.hk, co.nz, com.br, co.in, co.kr; an IP address, a single-label host or a host on a shared-hosting suffix the helper does not know (github.io, notion.site, wixsite.com, webflow.io) gives null, and null always falls back to the name key. Stored rows keep their old key until they are re-ingested; the dedupe repair in jobs-maintain then regroups them (no backfill statement: the hash cannot be recomputed in SQL).
ACCEPT: registrableDomain('https://careers.stripe.com/jobs/1') is 'stripe.com', of 'jobs.foo.co.uk' is 'foo.co.uk' and of 'acme.github.io' is null; inputs named 'Stripe' and 'Stripe, Inc.' that both resolve to stripe.com (one by its stated website, one through ctx.companyDomains) get the same dedupeKey; two inputs named 'Summit' with different stated domains get different keys; with no stated domain and no map entry every key is byte-identical to today's (the existing identity tests are unchanged).
TESTS: server/src/features/jobs/normalize/rules.test.ts (registrable domain table), server/src/features/jobs/normalize/normalizeProviderJob.test.ts (stated domain, map entry, neither).
FILES: server/src/features/jobs/normalize/identity.ts, server/src/features/jobs/normalize/company.ts, server/src/features/jobs/normalize/normalizeProviderJob.ts, their tests

[P0] JSearch rows: a posting whose only link is LinkedIn or Indeed is not ingested; a board-only link lives 21 days (JI-6; strategy M-3, 1.5; INTL note 8.1 M7, 8.2 S6)
CHANGE: server/src/features/jobs/normalize/normalizeProviderJob.ts (source step, 189-201): for aggregator providers (jsearch; the rule is written per provider in one table so it can be extended) classify the usable links (applyUrl and sourceUrl after safeUrl): when every link is on a LinkedIn host (isLinkedInHost) or on an Indeed host (the indeed brand pattern in server/src/features/jobs/normalize/ats.ts BOARD_BRANDS), set applyUrl to null and add the note 'linkedin_only_link' or 'indeed_only_link'; the ingest pipeline already drops a row without an apply URL and counts its notes (pipeline.ts 124-128), so the skip is counted with no pipeline change. A row that has an employer or ATS link next to a LinkedIn link keeps the employer link (MKT-J2 already prefers it). The existing note 'apply_url_linkedin_host' is no longer produced for ingest-eligible rows. server/src/features/jobs/normalize/identity.ts resolveExpiresAt (90-95): for provider jsearch, when the provider states no expiry and the chosen apply link is on a job-board or aggregator host (isJobBoardHost) the life is postedAt + 21 days (new constant AGGREGATOR_BOARD_LINK_DAYS = 21); a JSearch row whose link is on an employer or ATS host keeps 45 days (the board sync or the liveness check closes it earlier through the shared atsPostingKey). server/src/features/jobs/normalize/adapters.ts inputFromJSearchJob (100-150): stop reading is_direct for the apply link choice (use the same host rule as MKT-J2 through a shared helper exported from server/src/features/jobs/normalize/ats.ts: pickEmployerLink(urls)) so the raw-payload path and the client path agree.
ACCEPT: The 'Accepted when' of JI-6: a row whose only link is on linkedin.com is skipped and counted under 'linkedin_only_link' in the run notes; the same for an indeed.com-only row; a row linking to totaljobs.com is kept with expiresAt = postedAt + 21 days; a row linking to jobs.lever.co keeps 45 days and is marked direct; no LinkedIn URL reaches sourceUrl, originalHost or applyUrl of a stored row.
TESTS: server/src/features/jobs/normalize/normalizeProviderJob.test.ts (the four link cases, notes, expiry days), server/src/features/jobs/normalize/rules.test.ts (pickEmployerLink).
FILES: server/src/features/jobs/normalize/normalizeProviderJob.ts, server/src/features/jobs/normalize/identity.ts, server/src/features/jobs/normalize/adapters.ts, server/src/features/jobs/normalize/ats.ts, their tests

[P0] Expiry: a stated deadline is honoured for every source; the posting-age cut-off applies to aggregator rows only (JI-10, JT-2, JI-8; strategy M-22, 1.5)
CHANGE: Today server/src/features/jobs/normalize/identity.ts resolveExpiresAt returns null for every provider in NO_DATE_EXPIRY_PROVIDERS (line 82: both banks, user_import, ats_public), which also throws away a deadline the source states (Greenhouse application_deadline, 台灣就業通 STOP_DATE, USAJobs ApplicationCloseDate, a syndicated bank job's validity), and server/src/features/jobs/ingest/maintain.ts buildExpireSql (60-66) skips the same boards entirely. New rule in both places: (a) an explicit provider expiry (a valid date in or after 2000) is stored for every provider except user_import; (b) the default 'posted + N days' is applied only to aggregator providers: activejobs and activejobs_feed 45 days (until the vendor's expired feed closes them, MKT-J9), linkedin 45, jsearch 45 or 21 (previous item); (c) ats_public, both banks, tw_open_data, tw_gov_jobs and usajobs get no default: they close by listing diff, tombstone, sweep absence or their stated deadline. Rename the constant to AGE_EXPIRY_PROVIDERS (the aggregators) and derive the old list from it. buildExpireSql becomes: archive when "expiresAt" < now() for every sourceBoard, or when "expiresAt" IS NULL AND "postedAt" < now() - 45 days only for sourceBoard in the aggregator boards ('activejobs','linkedin','jsearch'); never by age for the rest. Keep closeReason 'expired'. Mainland naive timestamps: server/src/features/jobs/normalize/identity.ts toDate (44-55) gains an optional naiveOffsetMinutes and normalizeProviderJob passes 480 for market 'cn' sources that send zone-less strings (a zone-less '2026-10-11T09:00:00' from a mainland source is 01:00 UTC); a year of 0001 or before 2000 stays 'no date'.
ACCEPT: The 'a 300-day-old posting still listed by its board is ingested' line of JI-10: an ats_public input posted 300 days ago with no deadline has expiresAt null and survives buildExpireSql; the same input with application deadline next week gets that expiresAt and is archived after it passes; a tw_open_data input with STOP_DATE is archived the day after; a jsearch row without expiry is archived by age, an ats row never is; a zone-less mainland time is stored 8 hours earlier in UTC.
TESTS: server/src/features/jobs/normalize/normalizeProviderJob.test.ts and rules.test.ts (expiry table per provider, the naive-offset cases), server/src/features/jobs/ingest/maintain.test.ts (the new SQL through the snapshot or a string assertion; boards that expire only by date).
FILES: server/src/features/jobs/normalize/identity.ts, server/src/features/jobs/normalize/normalizeProviderJob.ts, server/src/features/jobs/ingest/maintain.ts, server/src/features/jobs/ingest/maintain.test.ts, the normalize tests

[P1] Carry-through fields for later sources: provider sponsorship reading, district, shift pattern (JI-7, JI-11, JT-7 preparation; strategy 1.5 "provider fields first")
CHANGE: MKT-J1 added the optional inputs; this item makes them reach the row so M3 bundles only have to set them. NormalizedJob (server/src/features/jobs/normalize/types.ts) gains sponsorshipProvider: 'offered' | 'not_offered' | null, locationDistrict: string | null and workShift: 'day' | 'evening' | 'night' | 'rotating' | 'part_time' | null. server/src/features/jobs/normalize/normalizeProviderJob.ts copies them (district trimmed, at most 40 characters; workShift only when it is one of the five values). server/src/features/jobs/ingest/upsert.ts writes three columns delivered by the M0 schema bundle: "locationDistrict" and "workShift" as EXCLUDED values; for sponsorship the rule is strict (D3, ruling C18): when the input carries a provider reading and the stored row has no posting quote (RAJob.sponsorshipEvidence IS NULL), set "sponsorship" to the reading and "sponsorshipSource" to 'provider:<provider id>'; a row whose sponsorship came from the posting's own words (sponsorshipSource 'posting_quote' or a non-null sponsorshipEvidence, written by enrichment) is never overwritten by a provider reading; when the provider stops stating a reading and the stored source is 'provider:…', both columns go back to NULL. Do not touch the enrichment writer (features/jobs/enrich, another owner): it keeps writing sponsorship with its quote; note in the handoff that it should also set sponsorshipSource = 'posting_quote'.

[P0] Taiwan district table (county code, 3-digit postal code, names) that drives the sweep (JT-2, JT-7 preparation; strategy 1.3; TW note 3.1, 5.3)

New server/src/features/jobs/geo/twDistricts.json { version, asOf, source: { name, publisher, url, license, retrievedOn }, counties: [{ code, name, nameAlt }], districts: [{ zip3, countyCode, county, district }] } and server/src/features/jobs/geo/twDistricts.ts (typed accessors: TW_COUNTIES, districtsOfCounty(code), districtByZip(zip3), findTwDistrict(text) which splits strings such as '新竹縣竹北市', '臺北市士林區' or '台中市不限' into county and district, accepting both 台 and 臺; validateTwDistricts for the test). The 22 county codes come from the interface document as listed in JOB_SOURCES_TW.md 3.1: 01 台北市, 31 新北市, 11 基隆市, 33 桃園市, 12 新竹市, 34 新竹縣, 35 苗栗縣, 13 台中市, 38 南投縣, 37 彰化縣, 39 雲林縣, 14 嘉義市, 40 嘉義縣, 15 台南市, 02 高雄市, 43 屏東縣, 32 宜蘭縣, 45 花蓮縣, 46 台東縣, 44 澎湖縣, 23 金門縣, 24 連江縣. The district rows must be built from an official published list (the open-data interface document if it carries the zipno table, otherwise 中華郵政's 3-digit postal code list), with the source URL, its licence and the retrieval date written into the file's source block; never type postal codes from memory (D3). If no official list can be retrieved in the session, commit the file with the 22 counties and an empty districts array and say so in the handoff: the sweep then uses its fallback split (next item) and ops supplies the list later. Export the module from server/src/features/jobs/geo/index.ts. Nothing here changes parseLocation or the city table (MKT-J14 adds the district level to job rows).

[P0] 台灣就業通 adapter: request, field mapping, pay only from the numeric fields (JT-2; strategy M-5, 1.3; TW note 3.1, 6 items 1-2)
CHANGE: Replace the guarded stub server/src/features/jobs/sources/twOpenData.ts (TW_OPEN_DATA_LICENCE_CONFIRMED false at line 24, twOpenDataStatus 33-38) with a JobSourceAdapter: provider 'tw_open_data' (declared in MKT-J1), kind 'cursor', markets ['intl'], sourceBoards ['tw_open_data'], costModel 'free', supportsCountry = TW only, dailyCallLimit null. The licence (政府資料開放授權條款 第1版) is confirmed by reading (strategy 8), so the adapter is ON by default: enabled unless TW_OPEN_DATA_JOBS_ENABLED is explicitly false / 0 / off; rewrite the header. Request: GET <TW_OPEN_DATA_JOBS_URL, default https://free.taiwanjobs.gov.tw/webservice_taipei/Webservice.ashx>?CITY=<code>&COUNT=1000&T=CSV, optionally &zipno=<3 digits> and &jobno=<2-digit 大類>; https only, redirect 'error', 20 s timeout, response cap 8 MB, header User-Agent = sourceUserAgent('intl', env) (MKT-J1). Parse the CSV with csv-parse; column headers carry the Chinese label in full-width brackets (for example 'OCCU_DESC（職務名稱）'): match on the ASCII part before the bracket. Mapping per row: title = OCCU_DESC; company = COMPNAME; description = JOB_DETAIL (plain text); applyUrl = sourceUrl = URL_QUERY (the vacancy page on job.taiwanjobs.gov.tw; the user applies there, D1); externalId = 'tw:<EMPLOYER_ID>:<HIRE_ID>' read from URL_QUERY's query string, and a row without both is skipped and counted (no_stable_id), never given an invented id; location = CITYNAME with locationCountry 'TW' (binding); employmentType from WK_TYPE (全職 -> full time, 兼職 -> part time); postedAt = TRANDATE (it is the update date: set postedAtEstimated true so cards say last verified, not posted); expiresAt = STOP_DATE (YYYYMMDD, end of that day in Taipei time, UTC+8); experience from EXPERIENCE ('無' / '不拘' -> 0 years, 'N年以上' -> minimum N); education from EDGRDESC through the education input the parity wave added (不拘 -> none, 專科 -> associate, 大學 -> bachelor, 碩士 -> master, 博士 -> phd, anything else unset); taxonomyId from CJOB2_COUNT through the 通俗職業 map (item 6); sourcePublisher '台灣就業通'. Pay: salaryMin / salaryMax ONLY from numeric NT_L / NT_U (currency TWD; period from SALARYCD: 月薪 and 部分工時(月薪) -> month, 時薪 -> hour, 日薪 -> day, 論件計酬 -> no period and no figure); when NT_L / NT_U are '-' or not numbers pass SALARYCD verbatim as salaryText with no figure (MKT-J1 made that sentence 'negotiable, no figure'). Never store or infer the statutory threshold. No logo, no contact fields, no English are available: leave them empty.
ACCEPT: With a fixture response: a 月薪 row gives 30,000-38,000 TWD a month, disclosed; the row whose SALARYCD is '依學經歷、證照核薪(每月經常性薪資達4萬元以上)' and whose NT_L / NT_U are '-' gives no figure, salaryDisclosed false and that text; STOP_DATE 20261231 gives expiresAt 2026-12-31T15:59:59Z; a row whose URL lacks HIRE_ID is skipped and counted; every input has provider country TW, publisher 台灣就業通 and the vacancy URL as apply link; with TW_OPEN_DATA_JOBS_ENABLED=false the adapter reports disabled and fetches nothing; no test touches the network.
TESTS: server/src/features/jobs/sources/twOpenData.test.ts with fixtures under server/src/features/jobs/sources/__fixtures__/tw/ (a few rows per shape: record them with one manual request to the open-data endpoint and trim to five rows, or, without network, hand-build them from the documented field list and mark the README SYNTHETIC): header matching, every mapping above, the skip tally, the kill switch, a non-200 answer and an oversized body return an error result without throwing.

[P0] Resumable sweep cursor (county -> district -> 大類), one sweep a day, closure after two complete sweeps without the row (JT-2; strategy 1.3, 1.5; critic C12)
CHANGE: A full sweep is a few hundred sequential requests and cannot finish in one 300 s function run. The adapter's standing query (created by ensureBankSyncQueries for every cursor adapter of the market) keeps params.cursor = JSON text { v: 1, sweepStartedAt, prevSweepStartedAt, lastCompleteSweepStartedAt, county: index into the 22 codes, zip: index or null, jobno: index or null, incomplete: boolean, counts }. One fetch performs at most TW_OPEN_DATA_REQUESTS_PER_FETCH requests (default 5), strictly sequential with TW_OPEN_DATA_PAUSE_MS between them (default 1500), then returns the rows read, the advanced cursor and exhausted: false; the ingest tick re-leases it while budget remains (MKT-J2 caps a cursor source's share of a tick), so the sweep resumes at the same county, district and 大類 on the next run. Split rule: request the county; when it returns 1,000 rows (the cap) discard nothing but walk that county's districts from twDistricts (zipno); when a district returns 1,000, walk the 22 大類 codes ('01'-'22') for that district with jobno; when a (district, 大類) leaf still returns 1,000, keep its rows, set incomplete true and count tw_capped_leaf. Fallback when the district table is empty: split a capped county by the 22 大類 instead and mark a still-capped leaf the same way. A request error leaves the cursor where it was (retry on the next fetch) and after three consecutive errors at the same position the sweep is marked incomplete and moves on. When the last county is done: if the sweep is not incomplete, store lastCompleteSweepStartedAt; the adapter then answers { jobs: [], calls: 0, exhausted: true } without any request until 24 h after sweepStartedAt, when a new sweep starts (TW_OPEN_DATA_SWEEP_HOURS, default 24). Closure: when a complete sweep ends and the previous complete sweep exists, rows with sourceBoard 'tw_open_data', market intl, visibility public, archivedAt null and lastSeenAt older than the start of the previous complete sweep were absent from two consecutive complete sweeps: return up to 5,000 of their externalIds as closedExternalIds with closeReason 'source_removed' (read through deps.db, the lazy Prisma import the ats_public adapter uses); an incomplete sweep closes nothing. Rows also expire on STOP_DATE through expiresAt (MKT-J4). Register the adapter: new server/src/features/jobs/sources/register.ts (side-effect module, idempotent like atsPublic/register.ts) registers tw_open_data; it is imported by server/src/features/jobs/sources/twHooks.ts, which server/src/features/jobs/marketHooks.ts imports statically, so the adapter is in the registry before any plan or ingest run.
ACCEPT: The 'Accepted when' of JT-2: a fixture sweep in which county 01 returns 1,000 rows is split by district, and a capped district by 大類; a run cut off after its request budget returns exhausted false and the next fetch resumes at the same county and district (the cursor round-trips through JSON); after a complete sweep the adapter makes no request for 24 h; a row seen in sweep 1 and absent from complete sweeps 2 and 3 is returned as closed at the end of sweep 3, and is not closed when sweep 3 was incomplete; requests are never concurrent and each carries the User-Agent; adaptersForBrand(roboapply) includes tw_open_data and adaptersForBrand(goapply) does not.
TESTS: server/src/features/jobs/sources/twOpenData.test.ts with a scripted fake fetch and fake clock: split decisions, resume, error handling, daily cadence, closure query (fake db) and the incomplete rule; a registry test that importing marketHooks registers the adapter once.
FILES: server/src/features/jobs/sources/twOpenData.ts, server/src/features/jobs/sources/twOpenData.test.ts, server/src/features/jobs/sources/register.ts (new), server/src/features/jobs/sources/twHooks.ts (new), server/src/features/jobs/marketHooks.ts

[P0] OGDL attribution on every open-data row, in the API and on the card (JT-2; strategy 1.3; TW note 3.1, 6 item 3)
CHANGE: The licence voids itself without attribution, and the constant in the stub is short of what its Exhibit asks for (provider, year, dataset name, licence statement). server/src/features/jobs/sources/twHooks.ts: a MarketHookSet with id 'tw_sources', appliesTo = market intl and sourceBoard in a table TW_OPEN_DATA_ATTRIBUTIONS keyed by sourceBoard: tw_open_data -> (year) => '資料來源：勞動部勞動力發展署 ' + year + '「台灣就業通網站職缺清單」，依政府資料開放授權條款第1版公開釋出'; tw_gov_jobs -> (year) => '資料來源：行政院人事行政總處 ' + year + '「行政院人事行政總處事求人機關徵才資料」，依政府資料開放授權條款第1版公開釋出' (dataset 7229; unused until MKT-J12 ships that adapter). cardMeta returns { attribution: { text, url: 'https://data.gov.tw/license' } } where year is the Taipei-time year of the row's lastSeenAt (or of now when the row has none); afterNormalize sets sourceName to the dataset's publisher label and leaves originalSourceName empty (the dataset is the original source). The sentences are data, not UI copy: they live in this server file in Traditional Chinese for every locale, and the 台灣就業通 logo is never used (trademarks are outside the licence). Add the set to MARKET_HOOK_SETS in server/src/features/jobs/marketHooks.ts (line 51). CHANGE: server/src/features/jobs/taxonomy/taxonomy.v1.json has en and zh only, so zh-TW users see English role names and Taiwan queries cannot be built. Add to every one of the 307 nodes a zhHant label, and to every role (level 3) synonyms.zhHant. These are translations in Taiwan usage, not conversions of the Simplified label: 軟體 (not 软件 / 軟件), 資料 (not 数据), 網路, 程式, 專案, 行銷, 人資, 韌體, 演算法, 產品經理, 工程師, 專員, 助理, 儲備幹部. Add at file level zhHantReview: { status: 'draft', reviewedBy: null, reviewedOn: null } (a Taiwan-native reviewer signs off later: owner item 19; the labels ship as draft because zh-TW otherwise shows English). server/src/features/jobs/taxonomy/taxonomy.ts: make zhHant required in TaxonomyNode now that the data has it; validateTaxonomy (125-149) requires a non-empty zhHant on every node; a test additionally checks every zhHant label and synonym against the terms the variant glossary bans for zh-TW (i18n/glossary/zh-variants.json, the list scripts/check-zh-variants.mjs enforces on bundles; the taxonomy file is not a bundle, so the test reads the glossary itself); taxonomyLabel(id, 'zh-TW') returns zhHant. server/src/features/jobs/taxonomy/match.ts: index the zhHant synonyms next to zh ones so a Traditional title matches without relying only on the variant folding. The planner (MKT-J3) reads node.zhHant for Taiwan queries.
ACCEPT: The 'Accepted when' of JT-4, first half: taxonomyLabel('software_engineer', 'zh-TW') returns '軟體工程師' and never a Simplified string; validateTaxonomy passes for the shipped file and fails for a node without zhHant; no zhHant label or synonym contains a term the glossary bans for zh-TW; a title '資深軟體工程師' maps to the software engineer role; exportTaxonomyLabels('zh-TW') has one entry per node; ids, en and zh labels and the node count (307) are unchanged; npm run check:zh-variants passes.

bundles.title: Provider health in the admin System panel: plan, remaining quota, days to reset, dead sources visible
items:
[P0] System status reports every provider of the served brands with its quota snapshot (JI-1; strategy 1.2 last paragraph; TW note 6 item 9)
CHANGE: server/src/features/admin/contract.ts ProviderUsageRow (92-100) gains: market ('intl' | 'cn', from the usage key: a ':cn' suffix is the mainland counter), plan: string | null, requestsLimit, requestsRemaining, jobsLimit, jobsRemaining (number | null), resetAt: string | null, daysToReset: number | null, observedAt: string | null, costModel: 'free' | 'per_job' | 'per_request', and state: 'ok' | 'low' | 'exhausted' | 'not_subscribed' | 'unauthorized' | 'gated' | 'disabled' | 'unknown'. server/src/features/admin/system.ts: SystemStore (line 53) gains providerQuota(): the AppConfig row 'jobs.providerQuota.v1' parsed with parseProviderQuota from MKT-J1's server/src/features/jobs/ingest/quotaContract.ts (read-only; this bundle never writes it: MKT-J2 does). The providers list is no longer 'rows that have usage today': build it from the source registry of every brand the deployment serves (the registry the parity wave added) so a provider with zero calls is still listed, then merge today's RAProviderUsage counters (including '<provider>:cn' rows) and the snapshot. State: snapshot state when it is exhausted / not_subscribed / unauthorized and its reset is in the future; 'low' when requestsRemaining is under 10% of requestsLimit; 'disabled' when the adapter reports disabled for another reason (no key, kill switch); 'gated' for a metered source that waits for a larger plan (jobsLimit known and under 20,000 for the licensed feed, the M-2 gate); 'ok' otherwise; 'unknown' with no snapshot for a metered provider. Unmetered sources (boards, banks, open data) show calls and yields only. server/src/features/admin/limits.ts keeps reading daily limits from the ingest area's exports.
ACCEPT: The 'Accepted when' of JI-1, panel half: with a stored snapshot { provider activejobs, plan BASIC, requestsLimit 25, requestsRemaining 0, resetAt 17 days ahead, state exhausted } GET /admin/system returns a row for activejobs with plan 'BASIC', requestsRemaining 0, daysToReset 17 and state 'exhausted' even though it made no call today; jsearch with 9,773 of 10,000 shows state ok; a provider absent from the snapshot shows state unknown and null numbers (never invented values); a GoApply-served deployment lists 'activejobs:cn' as its own row with market cn.
TESTS: server/src/features/admin/__tests__/services.test.ts with the fake SystemStore in fakes.ts (add providerQuota): merge of registry, usage and snapshot; every state; the ':cn' row; server/src/features/admin/__tests__/routes.test.ts: the response shape.

[P0] Quota gate and transports for the licensed feed (JI-7; strategy M-2, 1.2 tier 1, 7 item 1)
CHANGE: The feed must run by itself the day a paid plan exists and must not run on the free BASIC plan (25 requests, 250 jobs a month). server/src/features/jobs/ingest/quota.ts: feedGate(env, now) -> { open: boolean, reason: 'plan_too_small' | 'no_key' | 'disabled' | 'exhausted' | 'ok', monthlyJobs: number | null }. monthlyJobs = the larger of the stored snapshot's jobsLimit for provider 'activejobs' (MKT-J2 reads x-ratelimit-jobs-limit from every response) and env FANTASTIC_MONTHLY_JOBS (the plan size the owner bought, for a transport whose responses do not state it). The gate is open only when monthlyJobs >= 20,000 (constant FEED_MIN_MONTHLY_JOBS), a key for the chosen transport exists, FANTASTIC_FEED_DISABLED is not true and the snapshot is not exhausted. Daily job budget: INGEST_FEED_DAILY_JOBS, default floor(monthlyJobs / 31); jobs returned are counted in RAProviderUsage.jobsReturned under 'activejobs' (and 'activejobs:cn' for the mainland sync) and a fetch is refused once the day's jobs reach the budget. Transport in server/src/roboapply/v2/lib/raFantasticJobs.ts: add feedRequest(path, params, opts) next to the search call, sharing the breaker, timeout (25 s) and quota listener: 'rapidapi' (default; host active-jobs-db.p.rapidapi.com with RAPID_API_KEY, as today) or 'direct' when FANTASTIC_TRANSPORT=direct (host data.fantastic.jobs with FANTASTIC_API_KEY). The direct API's authentication header and exact paths are taken from the vendor's documentation (https://developer.fantastic.jobs/documentation/endpoints/new-jobs and /expired-jobs), read in the session and cited with the date in the file header; if they cannot be confirmed, the header name is read from FANTASTIC_API_KEY_HEADER with no default and the direct transport reports 'no_key' until it is set (never a guessed header). Paths default to '/active-ats' and '/expired-ats' (INTL note 6.2) and can be overridden with FANTASTIC_FEED_PATH / FANTASTIC_EXPIRED_PATH because the RapidAPI listing has renamed routes before (file header, lines 24-25 and 552-554). Keys are read per call and never logged. The admin System panel already shows state 'gated' for a plan under 20,000 (MKT-J7).
ACCEPT: The first 'Accepted when' clause of JI-7: with the snapshot of today's plan (jobsLimit 250) feedGate is closed with reason plan_too_small and no feed request is ever built; with jobsLimit 100,000 (or FANTASTIC_MONTHLY_JOBS=100000 and a key) it is open and the daily job budget is 3,225; FANTASTIC_FEED_DISABLED=true closes it; with FANTASTIC_TRANSPORT=direct and no header name configured the gate reports no_key; no key value appears in a log or error string.

[P0] Window-sync adapter: one backfill, then hourly windows paged by offset and resumed across cron runs (JI-7; strategy 1.2 tier 1; INTL note 6.2, 8.1 M5)
CHANGE: New server/src/features/jobs/ingest/adapters/fantasticFeed.ts: JobSourceAdapter with provider 'activejobs_feed' (declared in MKT-J1; it writes sourceBoard 'activejobs' and externalId 'activejobs:<id>', the same rows the search adapter addresses), kind 'cursor', markets ['intl','cn'], costModel 'per_job', isEnabledFor(market) = feedGate open (and, for cn, the mainland switch of item 6), isEnabled = the gate, dailyCallLimit null (it is metered in jobs by item 1, not in calls). The standing query's params.cursor is JSON { v: 1, phase: 'backfill' | 'hourly', window: '7d' | '1h', offset, highWater: ISO | null, lastHourlyAt, lastExpiredHourlyAt, lastExpiredDailyAt, lastExpiredMonthlyAt }. One fetch = one request: phase backfill -> time_frame=7d, limit=1000, offset; a full page (1,000 rows) answers exhausted false with offset + 1000 (so paging resumes on the next lease or the next cron run, under MKT-J2's per-tick share); a short page ends the backfill and switches to hourly. Phase hourly: when at least 60 minutes have passed since lastHourlyAt, request time_frame=1h&limit=1000 and page by offset the same way; highWater = the newest date_created seen; after an outage longer than the window (lastHourlyAt more than 2 h ago) send date_created_gte=highWater instead of relying on the 1 h window. Every request carries description_format=text and include_basic_organization_details=true and the location filter of item 4. Rows are mapped with inputFromFantasticJob (server/src/features/jobs/normalize/adapters.ts 39-95, extended in item 5) and returned as jobs; the pipeline upserts and dedupes them (K2 collapses a feed row onto a board row for the same posting). Register the adapter in server/src/features/jobs/ingest/providers.ts ensureBuiltinAdapters (19-31) and let adaptersForBrand include it for RoboApply after 'activejobs' (the on-demand search adapter stays for interactive use). server/src/features/jobs/ingest/planner.ts: while the feed gate is open, the activejobs SEARCH adapter plans no seo_seed tuples (the feed covers the breadth; a seed search would pay per job for rows the feed already returns).
ACCEPT: The second 'Accepted when' clause of JI-7: on a plan with at least 20,000 jobs a month an hourly window pages by offset (two fixture pages of 1,000 and 240 rows produce two requests with offset 0 and 1000, the first answering exhausted false); a run interrupted between the pages resumes at offset 1000 from the stored cursor; a second fetch within the hour makes no request; the backfill runs once and never again after the phase switched; with the gate closed the adapter is disabled, the planner plans nothing for it and runJobsIngest makes no feed call.
TESTS: server/src/features/jobs/ingest/adapters/fantasticFeed.test.ts with an injected transport and fake clock: phases, paging, resume from a serialised cursor, the hourly cadence, the outage high-water path, budget refusal; server/src/features/jobs/ingest/planner.test.ts: no seeds on the search adapter while the gate is open.

[P0] The vendor's expired feed closes our rows by id (JI-7; strategy 1.5 closure; INTL note 6.2, 7.2)
CHANGE: Today a feed row lives until posted + 45 days although the vendor rechecks every job daily. In server/src/features/jobs/ingest/adapters/fantasticFeed.ts, after the hourly new-jobs window is drained, the same fetch cycle runs the expired feed by its own clocks in the cursor: every hour expired?time_frame=1h; once a day after 01:00 UTC time_frame=1d (catches what an hourly run missed); once a month time_frame=1m (reconciliation). The endpoint returns vendor ids only: map each to externalId 'activejobs:<id>' and return them as closedExternalIds with closeReason 'source_removed' (the pipeline archives matching open rows of sourceBoard 'activejobs' and the upsert revives a row the vendor lists again). An expired id we never stored is ignored. Expired calls cost requests, not jobs: count them as calls. Rows of this provider keep the 45-day default expiry as a backstop (MKT-J4's rule for aggregators) and take the vendor's date_validthrough when it is stated.

[P1] Filters that keep the bill down: countries, and exclude_source only for an ATS we already cover with at least 200 enabled boards (JI-7; strategy 1.2 tier 1; critic C14; INTL note 6.2)
CHANGE: In the feed adapter's request builder: (1) location = an OR of full country names (the API wants names, not codes; use fantasticCountryName from server/src/roboapply/v2/lib/raFantasticJobs.ts, line 158, and the OR syntax the vendor's endpoint documentation gives) for the ISO codes in INGEST_FEED_COUNTRIES, default 'US,CA,GB,IE,DE,FR,NL,ES,IT,SE,AU,SG,TW' (the brand's markets per strategy 1.2 and 1.3; a tunable default: the owner trims it after measuring volume with the vendor's count endpoint). The mainland standing query (market cn) sends location = 'China' only. (2) exclude_source: an ATS is excluded only once our own seed for it holds at least 200 enabled boards (constant FEED_EXCLUDE_MIN_BOARDS = 200): count RACareerSiteSource rows with enabled true grouped by ats (one cheap query per fetch cycle, cached for 10 minutes) and map our ats ids to the vendor's source names ('greenhouse', 'lever.co', 'ashby', 'smartrecruiters', 'workable', 'recruitee', 'personio', as listed in INTL note 6.2; confirm each name against the vendor's documentation and keep the map in one table with the doc date). Below 200 the ATS is NOT excluded: its jobs on boards we have not discovered would otherwise come from neither side; K2 dedupe keeps the board row canonical for the ones we do read. (3) Agencies are not excluded (the product keeps them and labels them); organization_agency is not sent. (4) No title or taxonomy filter by default; INGEST_FEED_TAXONOMIES (comma list, vendor taxonomy names) is passed as the vendor's taxonomy filter when set, for a plan that needs a cap.

CHANGE: server/src/features/jobs/normalize/adapters.ts inputFromFantasticJob (39-95) already maps experience level, key skills, work arrangement, employment type, salary and the organisation website. Complete it for the feed payload (record a fixture from the vendor's documented sample, or from one real response once a plan exists; until then build server/src/features/jobs/normalize/__fixtures__/fantastic-feed.json from the documented field list and mark it SYNTHETIC in the fixtures README): (1) companyFacts.domain = domain_derived when present (it feeds the employer-domain dedupe key of MKT-J4) and industries / size / headcount when include_basic_organization_details returns them, each with source 'provider:activejobs'; (2) sponsorshipProvider from the vendor's visa-sponsorship flag (ai_visa_sponsorship: true -> 'offered', false -> 'not_offered', absent -> null): MKT-J4 stores it as sponsorship with sponsorshipSource 'provider:activejobs_feed' only when no posting quote exists, so it is always shown as the provider's reading and never as a fact; (3) taxonomyId: map the vendor's taxonomy labels (ai_taxonomies_a) to our tree through a small table in this file that contains ONLY labels seen in the fixture or the vendor's documentation, each mapped to an L1 / L3 id or to null; an unmapped label falls back to the title dictionary (never guess a mapping); (4) expiresAt from date_validthrough; postedAt from date_posted, else date_created with postedAtEstimated true; (5) applyIsDirect = source_type 'ats' (unchanged). CHANGE: server/src/features/jobs/sources/atsPublic/contract.ts PUBLIC_ATS (line 12) gains 'workable', 'recruitee', 'personio', 'lever_eu' (and 'beisen', item 6); PUBLIC_ATS_NAMES gains their display names (Workable, Recruitee, Personio, Lever, 北森: vendor names are data, not copy) and the client twin in components/features/market/tw/meta.ts follows. server/src/features/jobs/sources/atsPublic/http.ts: API_HOSTS (line 16) is an exact-host list; add apply.workable.com and api.eu.lever.co, and add a second, pattern-based rule for tenant hosts, each anchored and tested: ^[a-z0-9-]+\.recruitee\.com$, ^[a-z0-9-]+\.jobs\.personio\.(de|com)$ (and ^[a-z0-9-]+\.zhiye\.com$ only while the 北森 flag is on). assertApiHost refuses everything else before a request is sent; redirects stay refused (redirect 'error'), which is also the rule for Personio non-customers. Add getXml(url, deps) returning text under the same guards and a small tolerant reader in server/src/features/jobs/sources/atsPublic/xml.ts (elements by name, CDATA, entity decoding; no new dependency) for flat feeds. A board token for a tenant-host ATS is the sub-domain label and must match /^[a-z0-9-]{1,63}$/. Each connector implements AtsConnector (boardUrl, read with listOnly and known) and returns complete listings in one call, so MKT-J5's sync, closure diff, market split and discovery work unchanged; candidates that discovery stored for 'workable' and 'lever_eu' are now validated by the same step. server/src/features/jobs/sources/atsPublic/shared.ts externalIdFor and the sourceBoard = ats convention are unchanged, so K2 keys from MKT-J4 ('workable:slug:shortcode', 'lever_eu:site:uuid') agree with the rows.
